subject.title: [Bug]: Z.AI Coding-Plan: ECONNRESET triggers model fallback — fallback notice is invisible to the user in async contexts (cron jobs, sub-agents, isolated runs)

question: Should OpenClaw surface model fallback notices from async child, cron, and isolated runs to the triggering user's visible output, and should per-provider connection/dispatcher knobs be accepted as a public config surface?
rationale: The notice audience intersects an opposing open leakage concern, and the requested connection policy would add security-sensitive provider transport config beyond the current headers/auth/proxy/TLS surface.

options.title: Land async notices only
options.body: Accept parent/result fallback notice propagation as the bug fix while keeping transport knobs out of this issue until a separate design is approved.

options.title: Require a notice audience gate
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define which channels and async surfaces may receive model routing notices.

options.title: Design full transport policy
options.body: Treat this as a broader provider reliability project with explicit SSRF, upgrade, and config-schema review before implementation.

recommendation.title: Land async notices only
recommendation.body: Accept parent/result fallback notice propagation as the bug fix while keeping transport knobs out of this issue until a separate design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent source history shows steipete on the current fallback, provider request, transport, ACP relay, and cron helper files that define both sides of this decision.
